significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the conclusion that, for content-identical numeral-heavy problems, "more fragmented numerals cause a model to think longer" at equal accuracy and that this tax is partly caused by a "fragmentation-sensitive length/difficulty signal read at the prompt boundary BEFORE reasoning begins"; this combines a form-(iii) monotonic relation with form-(ii) causal mediation and establishes both a phenomenon and mechanism. It predicts reasoning-length changes under numeral re-encoding and explains some inefficient budget allocation, although its explicit restriction to "numeral-heavy reasoning, not all natural-language tasks" makes it a consequential side mechanism rather than a general law of efficient reasoning; Singh and Strouse's 2024 work, "Tokenization Counts: The Impact of Tokenization on Arithmetic in Frontier LLMs," confirms that numeral segmentation is already consequential for model behavior, while work such as "s1: Simple Test-Time Scaling" makes unnecessary reasoning-token allocation operationally relevant. The branches are determinate: failure of Claim 1 rules out the matched-accuracy compute tax, while failure of Claim 2 rejects the prompt-boundary budget account even if the behavioral effect remains, so both nulls constrain explanations. In the topic-substitution check, generic "efficient reasoning from a mechanistic perspective" would not supply this fragmentation-to-budget law or boundary mediation, so the score reflects claim-specific content rather than the topic.

reach.justification: The principal handle is the claim's "deployable, training-free input-side fix" of "re-encoding the same numbers into fewer, cleaner tokens"; it is ex ante because preprocessing occurs before reasoning and can reduce latency and serving cost before excess tokens are generated. After tokenizer-specific measurement or re-extraction, the conclusion still predicts a monotonic fragmentation–reasoning-length relation and the boundary condition that models with "clean single-digit tokenization may show no effect," rather than merely offering an uncommitted procedure for searching. Its asserted scope is appropriately limited to numeral-heavy reasoning, but downstream users include evaluation-harness designers, inference-serving practitioners, tokenizer designers, and reasoning-distillation researchers, giving uptake beyond the interpretability researchers who identify the mechanism. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the broad topic alone supplies neither the numeral-reformatting handle nor its pre-outcome action window and tokenizer-dependent prediction.
